item.title: Jordan Normal Form and Defective Matrices
item.description:
When a matrix is not diagonalizable (fewer than $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors), Jordan normal form still gives a nearly diagonal representation using generalized eigenvectors.

Generalized eigenvectors

$\mathbf{v}$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $k$ for eigenvalue $\lambda$ if

$$ (A - \lambda I)^k \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0} \quad \text{and} \quad (A - \lambda I)^{k-1} \mathbf{v} \neq \mathbf{0} $$

Ordinary eigenvectors are rank 1. Generalized eigenvectors extend the idea when $\text{GM} < \text{AM}$.
